incremental_scope: Native SQL PREPARE/EXECUTE for unchanged complete pinned pg_dump/pg_restore, preserving exact-source parser admission and connection-local provenance.

findings.title: ExecuteStmt includes CREATE TABLE AS EXECUTE
findings.evidence: Read-only real parser probe for CREATE TABLE t AS EXECUTE p returned statementFamilies=[ExecuteStmt], with CREATE as first token. EXPLAIN EXECUTE returned ExplainStmt.
findings.required_behavior: Require the expected leading PREPARE/EXECUTE token plus the immediately following admissible native-name token and exact singleton ordered family list. A sole ExecuteStmt family alone does not enforce the specified nested-form exclusion.
findings.resolution: Root explicitly accepted this classifier requirement before final review; the frozen spec already requires CREATE AS EXECUTE denial.

findings.title: Deduplicated production IDs do not establish one statement
findings.evidence: Repeated PREPARE and repeated EXECUTE probes each returned two identical entries in statementFamilies; Report.lean erases duplicate production IDs.
findings.required_behavior: Check list cardinality, not set equality. Continue using all production IDs and tokens for nested opaque and lexical-mode policy checks.
findings.resolution: Root explicitly accepted ordered singleton-family classification.

findings.title: Body extraction and native name resolution are trusted adapter work
findings.evidence: bodyPart establishes a nonempty substring relation. nativeExecute takes a supplied target name and an admitted request/report. Neither definition derives syntax, the target name or SQL case folding from source bytes.
findings.required_behavior: Do not claim these theorems prove SQL identifier normalization, statement classification or body-span extraction. Use parser token byte offsets against original UTF-8 bytes, retain whole accepted source, and validate boundary/name restrictions in runtime tests.
findings.resolution: The model comments and frozen formal_scope retain the adapter boundary; root confirmed body-span extraction remains trusted runtime work.

positive_assessments: The observed strict revision 3 failure is preserved as a real failed recovery gate. Supporting parsed static PREPARE/EXECUTE addresses native utility behavior without bypassing the parser or dropping backup ACL content.

Every native PREPARE and EXECUTE must have its own complete exact-source grammar acceptance. The prepared query is inside the admitted PREPARE source; no arbitrary SQL string execution, placeholder rewriting or parameter-to-SQL promotion is introduced.

ASCII-only names limited to 63 bytes avoid PostgreSQL quoted-name, Unicode and truncation ambiguity. SQL names are folded only for lookup; original wire SQL remains unchanged and protocol names retain exact bytes.

A shared connection-local accepted statement namespace supports SQL-to-protocol Bind and protocol-to-SQL EXECUTE while preserving immutable portal provenance. Unknown targets must fail and successful backend execution is not inferred from optimistic state.
Cache decisions are immutable classification metadata only. A cache hit does not create a prepared statement on a new connection or bypass EXECUTE target lookup.

All existing opaque-body, mode-change, expression-policy and resource restrictions continue inside PREPARE bodies and EXECUTE arguments. The changed native policy does not authorize DO, function/procedure bodies, nested execution forms, DEALLOCATE, prepared transactions or legacy fast-path calls.

formal_assessment.conclusion: The abstract extensions express own-request and known-target acceptance, shared provenance for Bind, cache nonmutation and nonvacuous native traces. They preserve reachable_wellFormed for the added nativePrepared constructor.
formal_assessment.required_before_production_changes: Complete all six exact-hash seats and the planned two clean formal builds bound to this final revision 4 hash. Prior revision 3 proof evidence is not revision 4 closure.

runtime_acceptance_required: Real native PREPARE/EXECUTE with folded ASCII names, current-connection and unknown-target behavior, duplicate-name/backend-error traces and both cross-protocol directions.
Warm cache reused on a different connection must not establish a target; closing a prepared object must remove its lookup authority even if classification is cached.
Quoted/Unicode/overlong names, repeated same-family statements, EXPLAIN EXECUTE and CREATE TABLE AS EXECUTE must fail before forwarding.
Unsafe set_config or other forbidden constructs in PREPARE bodies and EXECUTE arguments must fail; harmless SQL-looking literals remain data.
SQL prepared statements must consume existing per-connection object/metadata limits and preserve portal snapshots across accepted namespace changes.
Run full native pg_dump/pg_restore with ACLs, distinct client counters and canonical endpoints; retain revision 3 failure evidence and rerun migration/recovery preservation checks.
